body.statement: For each fixed \(c>0\) and \(v\in\{\mathrm w,+\}\), the nonempty fiber \(\{\Delta:(\log c,\Delta)\in\Theta_v(P)\}\) is an interval whose infimum and supremum equal the optimal values of the two linear semidefinite programs over \(\mathcal F_c^v(P,\Delta)\). Endpoint inclusion is equivalent to the separate feasibility tests in \(\mathrm{def{:}endpoint\text{-}attainment\text{-}test}\); neither inclusion is inferred from closed PSD constraints alone.
body.justification: Sharp numerical bounds require correct treatment of nonattainment on open-support moment faces.
body.gap: The grid program reports numerical endpoints but does not separate sharp infima and suprema from endpoint inclusion under continuous heterogeneity.
body.consumer: An applied researcher can report open, closed, or half-open APE bounds rather than silently treating every solver value as attainable.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(P,c,v\) and suppose the fiber is nonempty.  Write
\(z_{\mathrm w}=(m,a,b)\) and \(z_+=(m,a,b,t)\).  With \(c\) fixed, every
matrix entry in the defining blocks is affine in \((z_v,\Delta)\), and all
cell and APE restrictions are affine equalities.  Hence
\[
 \mathcal G_v(P,c)=\{(z_v,d):z_v\in\mathcal F_c^v(P,d)\}
\]
is convex.  Its linear image on the \(d\)-coordinate is therefore an interval.
By \(\mathrm{thm{:}exact\text{-}feedback\text{-}cone}\), this image is exactly
\(\{d:(\log c,d)\in\Theta_v(P)\}\), not merely an outer approximation.

The objective is bounded.  Indeed, for
\(\phi_c(u)=(c-1)u/((1+u)(1+cu))\), differentiation gives
\[
 \frac{d}{du}\frac{u}{(1+u)(1+cu)}
 =\frac{1-cu^2}{(1+u)^2(1+cu)^2}.
\]
Thus the maximum absolute effect is attained at \(u=c^{-1/2}\), and
\[
 |\phi_c(u)|\le\frac{|\sqrt c-1|}{\sqrt c+1}.
\]
Since \(\mu\) is a probability measure, the same bound holds for every
feasible \(d\).  Consequently the two explicit linear semidefinite programs
are
\[
 L_c^v(P)=\inf_{d,z_v}\{d:(z_v,d)\in\mathcal G_v(P,c)\},
 \qquad
 U_c^v(P)=\sup_{d,z_v}\{d:(z_v,d)\in\mathcal G_v(P,c)\}.
\]
Their values are precisely the sharp infimum and supremum by the exact-cone
equivalence.  An infimum belongs to the fiber exactly when some
\(z_v\in\mathcal F_c^v(P,L_c^v(P))\) exists, and the analogous statement with
\(U_c^v(P)\) proves upper inclusion.  These are the two separate tests in
\(\mathrm{def{:}endpoint\text{-}attainment\text{-}test}\).  Although each
lift is given by closed positive-semidefinite constraints, its projection on
\(d\) need not be closed; therefore closedness of the blocks alone proves
neither endpoint test.
